key_pathways: Renal excretion (glomerular filtration and active tubular secretion)

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Probenecid
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Probenecid inhibits renal tubular secretion of acyclovir, significantly increasing serum concentrations and nephrotoxicity risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use or monitor renal function closely if co-administration necessary; consider dose reduction

avoid_supplements.name: Nephrotoxic supplements (Aristolochic acid-containing herbs)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Combined nephrotoxicity with acyclovir increases risk of acute kidney injury, especially in elderly or renally compromised patients
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid supplements containing aristolochic acid or other nephrotoxic botanicals; monitor serum creatinine

caution_supplements.name: L-lysine
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential additive antiviral effects; limited clinical evidence but theoretical benefit in herpes prophylaxis
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for enhanced efficacy; no dose adjustment typically needed but inform patient of concurrent use

caution_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 induction may theoretically reduce acyclovir levels slightly, though acyclovir is minimally hepatically metabolized
caution_supplements.action: Counsel patient on limited interaction risk; monitor clinical response to antiviral therapy

caution_foods.name: High sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Excessive sodium intake may affect renal function and fluid balance, potentially impacting acyclovir clearance in susceptible patients
caution_foods.action: Maintain adequate hydration and counsel patients with renal impairment to moderate sodium intake

caution_foods.name: Dehydrating beverages (excessive caffeine/alcohol)
caution_foods.mechanism: Dehydration reduces glomerular filtration rate and increases acyclovir concentration, raising nephrotoxicity risk
caution_foods.action: Encourage adequate water intake (2-3 liters daily) and limit caffeinated/alcoholic beverages during treatment

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum creatinine, BUN, and urinalysis baseline and during therapy, particularly in elderly patients, those with renal impairment, or receiving IV acyclovir. Ensure adequate hydration to minimize nephrotoxicity risk and optimize renal clearance.
